name: Momus
label: Creation
lede: Nick Currie named himself after the Greek god of mockery, made five albums of clever, filthy synth-pop for Creation, got sued by a tyre company and a synthesizer pioneer, and wrote the line about everyone being famous for fifteen people.

eras.title: From Paisley to 4AD to Brel
eras.text: Nick Currie was born in Paisley in 1960, boarded at Edinburgh Academy while his father taught English in Athens, and took his stage name from the Greek god of mockery. Before he was Momus he was a member of a band on 4AD.

years.h: Currie joins ex-Josef K players in the Happy Family
years.p: The band puts out a single and an album, The Man on Your Street: Songs of the Dictator Hall, on 4AD.

years.src: Wikipedia: Momus · Wikipedia: The Poison Boyfriend
years.h: Bible stories, acoustic guitar: Circus Maximus
years.p: The first Momus album, on él, is stripped down and biblical. The same year he records the Nicky EP of Jacques Brel translations and writes about Brel at length for the New Statesman.

eras.title: McGee's tender pervert
eras.text: Alan McGee signed Momus to Creation Records, and over three albums the cabaret songwriter turned into a synth-pop provocateur writing about sex, AIDS-era Britain and Thatcher. The music press mostly loved it.

years.h: A full band, and voyeurs, on The Poison Boyfriend
years.p: Julian Standen produces the first Creation album, half Leonard Cohen-style song cycle, half drum machines. NME ranks it No. 39 of 1987.

years.h: McGee talks Momus out of his album title
years.p: McGee feared Creation's Canadian distributor, PolyGram, would refuse it. Released as Tender Pervert, it was partly Currie's answer to homophobic press coverage during the AIDS crisis.
years.xp:
AllMusic's Steve Huey called it "the first great Momus album." Sounds praised its "uncomfortable strength and purity."

Thomi Wroblewski's cover, Currie with two fingers raised like horns against flowers, later fed into [[Primal Scream|55704c38-224f-4b75-b29f-d43653f8bc9a]]'s album artwork. Kirin J. Callinan covered the title track in 2019.

years.src: Wikipedia: Don't Stop the Night · Wikipedia: Momus
years.h: 'The Hairstyle of the Devil' makes No. 94
years.p: His only UK chart single, in spring 1989, and a hit on San Francisco's Live 105. Stuart Maconie gave the album 9/10 in NME.
years.xp: Currie called Don't Stop the Night his "most British album": Thatcher's Britain, yuppies, AIDS. Maconie wrote that "only a fool could ignore this record." Rough Trade put it out in Germany.

eras.title: Rubber, Tokyo and a stormed office
eras.text: Momus found a second audience in Japan, fell out with Michelin, and made his last two Creation records as the label turned toward guitars. The run ended with a family crisis that reached the Creation office.

years.h: Flipper's Guitar invite Momus to Japan
years.p: The visit starts his long run with Tokyo's Shibuya-kei scene. Cornelius and the Poison Girlfriend, named after his 1987 album, come out of that circle.

years.big: "In the future everyone will be famous for fifteen people."
q: In the future everyone will be famous for fifteen people.
years.h: Momus updates Warhol's fifteen minutes
years.p: Said in 1991, years before blogs. The internet turned it into a saying of its own.

years.h: Michelin objects; unsold Hippopotamomus copies are destroyed
years.p: 'Michelin Man' turned the Bibendum mascot into a rubber fetish. Michelin threatened legal action; the song came off later pressings and the sleeve was changed.
years.xp:
NME's Betty Page gave the album 0/10 and called Momus a "perv"; Select's Ted Kessler found it "wickedly seductive." A 1991 documentary, Amongst Women Only, looked at the accusations of misogyny.

The words reappeared as 'Made of Rubber' in his 1992 lyric book Lusts of a Moron. Cherry Red's 2018 Recreate box restored the song and its title.

years.h: A Mishima play sends Voyager into ambient house
years.p: Seeing a Yukio Mishima play at the 1991 Edinburgh Festival shaped the record. NME gave it 2/10; Melody Maker's Simon Price called the change "revolutionary."

years.h: Jarvis Cocker writes asking Momus to produce Pulp
years.p: His 1980s albums reached the coming Britpop crowd. He also championed Suede early, through friendship with [[Brett Anderson|e6694ef2-d670-461b-a77b-f51f81faaf8f]] and Justine Frischmann.

years.h: Timelord is his last Creation album
years.p: Made while his teenage girlfriend, Shazna Nessa, was being held to an arranged marriage. Currie left Creation after her brothers stormed the label's offices, and signed to Cherry Red.
years.xp:
Currie produced and engineered it himself; Nippon Columbia released it in Japan, his first major-label album. NME's Stephen Dalton praised its "dry wit" but found it "emaciated."

With help from the British High Commission, the two married in 1994; Wikipedia says he was 34 and she was 17, and that they had first written to each other when she was 14. They separated in 1997 and divorced in 1999.

eras.title: A Number One, a lost eye, a $22 million suit
eras.text: A song he wrote for someone else became his first big commercial hit. Then came an infection that took the sight in one eye, and a lawsuit from Wendy Carlos that he paid off with songs.

years.h: Kahimi Karie takes his 'Good Morning World' to No. 1
years.p: Currie wrote it for Kahimi Karie, and it went to No. 1 in Japan with a heavily played TV ad. Wikipedia calls it his first big commercial hit.

years.h: The Philosophy of Momus starts the Cherry Red years
years.p: His first album after Creation. Slender Sherbet follows the same year, re-recording older songs.

years.h: A contact lens infection takes the sight in his right eye
years.p: Acanthamoeba keratitis, caught on holiday in Greece. Surgery helped, and the eyepatch and dark glasses became part of how he's photographed.

years.h: Wendy Carlos sues over 'Walter Carlos' for $22 million
years.p: The song on The Little Red Songbook imagined Carlos marrying her pre-transition self. They settled out of court: the song came off later CDs and Momus owed $30,000 in legal fees.

years.h: Fans commission songs about themselves to pay the lawyers
years.p: Stars Forever is a set of paid-for musical portraits in the style of 'Walter Carlos', a crowdfunding album before the word.

eras.title: Click Opera and the long tail
eras.text: Momus moved online early, kept a daily blog that became a landmark of the blogging era, then novels, then a memoir. The albums kept coming, roughly one a year.

yt: In his New York home studio, 2002
years.h: Click Opera starts on LiveJournal
years.p: A daily essay blog that ran until his 50th birthday, February 10, 2010. It led to columns for the New York Times and Wired.

years.h: Novelist: The Book of Scotlands and The Book of Jokes
years.p: The Book of Scotlands is shortlisted for the Scottish Arts Council's First Book prize.

years.h: Cherry Red boxes the Creation years
years.p: Procreate (2017) and Recreate (2018), with notes by Anthony Reynolds, bring 'Michelin Man' back under its own name.

years.h: Vivid and a memoir told by famous ghosts
years.p: Vivid logs the pandemic and his suspected case of COVID-19. Farrar, Straus & Giroux publish Niche, his life in fake eyewitness statements from historical figures.

years.h: Two more albums: Quietism and Acktor
years.p: Currie, now splitting his time between Berlin and Paris, is about 40 albums in.
